- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to match sentiment momentum.  
- After sharp price spikes, model often overshoots and fails to correct — reduce forecast slope after peak to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤ -0.5) and price drops, model frequently undercorrects — add a small downward bias to forecast to reflect sentiment.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish — adjust upward by 1–2% for such cases.  
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile, model tends to smooth too much — allow for 1–2% asymmetric jitter around forecast to capture sentiment-driven volatility.  
- In periods of strong mean reversion (e.g., price drops after sustained rise), model often fails to recognize the reversal — add a slight downward bias to forecast to reflect reversion.
